name: Sensibilité (the cult of sensibility)
plain_explanation: An eighteenth-century French fashion for direct, violent, unreasoned emotion, especially sympathy -- being moved to tears by a single destitute peasant family while remaining cold to systematic schemes to help peasants as a class.
precise_definition: A cultivated proneness to emotion, valued for its intensity and spontaneity rather than for being informed by thought or directed toward effective action.
why_it_mattered: It is the direct precursor and raw material of the romantic movement proper, which Rousseau inherited and gave wider scope.
historical_origin: Fashionable among cultivated people in eighteenth-century France before Rousseau.
examples: Weeping over a single poor family while ignoring structural poverty
The idealized 'poor' of romantic imagination who always have 'a few paternal acres' and lose them pathetically
competing_positions: Prudence and restraint as the supreme virtues, dominant from 1660 to Rousseau
influence_on_later_thinkers: Feeds directly into Rousseau's ethics and into the wider romantic revolt against convention.
connection_to_politics_or_religion: Associated with sympathy for the rural poor as a class, later displaced by the nineteenth-century idea of the urban/industrial proletariat.
